newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU-Russia summit set for Moscow on March 3.
newsitem.headline: EU-Russia summit set for Moscow on March 3.

text.p: A European Union-Russia summit postponed because of President Boris Yeltsin's ill-health will take place in Moscow on March 3, a European Commission spokesman said on Friday.
The summit was originally due to be held on February 4 in The Hague, but Yeltsin had not recovered sufficiently from a bout of pneumonia following his heart operation.
"We have just heard that this will take place on March 3 in Moscow," Commission spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas told a news conference.

The European Union will be represented by Commission President Jacques Santer, the Commissioner responsible for external relations Hans van den Broek, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo.
The two sides are expected to discuss trade, political relations, investment and development as well as the fight against drugs and money laundering.
Although they are likely to touch upon Russian opposition to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's expansion plans, the EU has been keen to keep its own enlargement a separate issue.

Yeltsin's illness has significantly interfered with a series of internmational meetings the Russian president was supposed to have held over the past six months and has raised speculation over his future at home.
